4 out of 10
A Tenkaichi turd with sprinkles on it.

Sure, the game looks great, but it lacks in almost everything else:

- No crossplay.
No crossplay in 2025 is a bad choice in this day and age. It heavily limits the community's connection.

- Half-baked story mode.
Story mode has some cool ideas, but doesn't quite follow through all the way with them. It feels rushed and therefore, having been poorly executed.

- Shallow fighting system.
Fights get very repetitive and they all feel the same, no matter what characters you use with the exceptions of Giants or super cheesy character like U.I. Goku / Super Vegito.

Overall,
This game gets 4 out of 10 .
It doesn't live up to the hype or its potential for a 2025 Dragon Ball game. The fights just devolve into a cheese-fest with hardly any dynamics or skill involved. The game is very pretty, but that's about it.

I used to like this game, i really did. Even with all of it's issues like lack of single player content, lack of updates, overpriced DLCs and sweaty online playerbase i really enjoyed it. I even considered it a worthy successor even with all of it's problems. My overall verdic on my older review used to be was that besides all it's issues this was still a fun game and a worthy successor to the Tenkaichi series espacially at a fat sale.

But then Sparking Neo was announced and released and this is where i lost all respect i had for this game. 35 bucks for content that should have been in the game ALREADY with reused assets being the cherry of top of this predatory cake and a below average roguelike mode. Bandai really charged us 70 for a BETA all this time and starved us until this very moment. And even worse, they thought they were sneaky when they lowered the price from 70 to 50. Bandai's greed really has no bounds.

Overall, fuck this game. I'm done. This is inexcusable no matter if you are a fan of this game or not. And if you are about to defend this predatory bs with "ItS 35 BuCkS" sensierly, please remove Bandai's foot off your mouth. It's gross and you deserve better than this.

I was hyped for this game when it first was announced but once the price tag was revealed I just knew it wouldn't be good. This is not a successor or sequel to Budokai Tenkaichi 3 but a pale imitation to what was once a fun and a core childhood memory to most. Sparking Zero is just a boring and uninteresting mess of a game, it was clearly a cash grab and many fell for it. If it turns out that you like watching the same movie length animations over and over then you might like this game. Now Tenkaichi 3 also suffered from being repetitive and had pretty lengthy animations at times, but the game had soul to it, and this does not.

One thing I learned about long dead franchises is that if they died a long time ago, then they should stay that way, as any new modern spin on an existing franchise that is loved by so many will just be ruined by corporate greed.

reason.text: Negative reviews focus on buying the Ultimate Edition and then having to pay extra for the NEO DLC, which reviews say should have been in the base game.
Reviews also tie this to the edition being delisted, and an official announcement from the same month covers the NEO release.

tldr.text: Very Positive (84%): recent reviews are lower at 74%, so the mood has cooled.
Players love the story and characters, yet that same theme draws the most complaints, with the price close behind.

details.text: A flagged review bomb in July pushed the monthly score down to 37%, so buyers today should treat that dip with caution.
Brand-new players are the least positive at 67%, while veteran players sit at 70%, so the mood is weaker at both ends than in the middle.
